title: Tomorrow Protocol
description: The executable design for the next day. Three caps are structural rather than advisory. missions has maxItems 3, so a fourth mission cannot be written however enthusiastic the session was. Every mission requires a non-empty success_condition, so a mission that cannot be answered yes or no tomorrow evening cannot be recorded. identity_challenge is a single object rather than an array, so there is exactly one per day and two is not expressible. Non-negotiables require active true, so a lapsed anchor cannot be listed as one to apply pressure. A zero-mission day is legal and must declare itself a rest day with a reason, which keeps an honest empty protocol distinct from an unfinished one.

missions.description: At most three. A list of seven produces a day of triage and an evening of explanations.

non_negotiables.description: Only the anchors currently in force. Each item requires active true, so an inactive one cannot appear here at all.

rest_day.description: A deliberate zero-mission day. The non-negotiables still stand.

rest_reason.description: Required on a rest day, so an honest empty protocol is distinguishable from an unfinished one

capacity_note.description: Why the mission count matches the real day, for example eleven hours of client obligations

allOf.description: Zero missions is legal, and it declares itself.
A rest day carries no missions. The two cannot both be asserted.

mission.description: One concrete action a stranger could execute, serving a named objective, answerable yes or no tomorrow evening

action.description: Ship the auth fix and deploy it. Not: work on the build.

why.description: The objective or contradiction this serves. A mission with no why is someone else's day leaking in.

success_condition.description: The observable state that makes tomorrow's answer a yes or a no. Required and non-empty: a mission without one is not a mission.

carried_from.description: Set when this mission was already written for an earlier day

condition.description: The binary condition. Met or not met, with no partial credit and no commentary.

active.description: Only currently active anchors are listable. An inactive one is not a non-negotiable, and a repeatedly broken one is a contradiction rather than an anchor.

identity_challenge.description: Exactly one per day. An object rather than an array, so a second challenge is not expressible.

why_uncomfortable.description: The friction that makes it a vote rather than a task

achievable_today.description: It starts and finishes inside tomorrow. Anything larger is a project and belongs elsewhere.

optional_challenge.description: Included only when it adds genuine value tomorrow. Omission is the normal case.

adds_value_because.description: Required. A challenge that cannot say what it adds is decoration and is dropped.

kill_reason.description: Killing a loop is a legitimate outcome and is recorded as a decision, not as a failure

carried_forward_count.description: Three untouched carry-forwards make this pattern input for the contradiction engine
